newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate eases to 10.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate eases to 10.3 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate eased 10 basis points to 10.3 percent on Thursday in livelier trade due to increased demand.
Dealers said settlements more than doubled to 50.2 million kuna but were still overshot by supply as lenders and borrowers failed to agree on terms.
Rates were steady, with a minimum of 9.0 percent charged by insurers for short-term loans. The interbank rates ranged between 10 percent call money and 15 percent for 90-day funds.

As a period of good banking sector liquidity continued, overnight borrowings shrank to 26.3 million kuna on Wednesday. Only one of four banks had a shortfall and others sought funds to maintain their statutory giro-account reserve.

The central bank stayed out of the foreign exchange market. Its kuna midrates for Friday's trade firmed to 5.3420 against the dollar while easing to 3.5682 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
